findings.description: storage_encrypted is set to false, so the RDS MySQL instance and its underlying storage/snapshots hold data in cleartext, exposing sensitive data if the storage layer or a snapshot is accessed.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, dramatically expanding the attack surface of the database (its endpoint is also exposed via an output).

The master username is the default 'admin' and the password is supplied via a plain Terraform variable, which is written in cleartext to the Terraform state and reused directly in EC2 user data, risking credential disclosure.
No parameter enforcing TLS (e.g. require_secure_transport) or IAM authentication is configured, so MySQL clients may connect over unencrypted channels to a publicly reachable database.
The MySQL 8.0 parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, allowing cleartext database connections to the instance it is attached to.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the EC2 instance role; any compromise of the internet-facing web instance yields full control of S3 data, EC2 (including privilege escalation via instance profile passing/user data) and RDS across the account.

The user_data script embeds the database username and password in cleartext; EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service (IMDSv1 is not disabled) and via ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, leaking DB credentials.

No metadata_options block requiring IMDSv2 (http_tokens = "required"), so an SSRF or local compromise on this web server can trivially retrieve the instance profile credentials backing the wildcard s3/ec2/rds policy.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the instance volume containing the plaintext dbinfo.inc credentials file may be stored unencrypted.

Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, permitting unrestricted outbound traffic that facilitates data exfiltration or command-and-control from a compromised resource.

findings.issue_category: missing egress restrictions / cleartext service exposure
findings.description: The RDS security group combines with publicly_accessible = true on the database; while ingress is limited to the VPC CIDR, the group has no description or restrictive egress and defines the network boundary for a publicly addressable database.
